notes: **2026-08-30** — (branch `ci/minutes-diet`, off master 6c8f1401; no schema change; follow-on to the CI cut below) — **E2E NOW STARTS FROM RAILWAY'S DEPLOY SIGNAL, NOT THE MASTER PUSH — THE ~320s OF PAID SLEEP IS GONE.** This was option 1 of the four priced in ci.yml's e2e header, and the only one that gives up nothing. ⚠️ **THE DESIGN'S ASSUMED MECHANISM WAS UNNECESSARY.** It called for wiring a Railway webhook to `repository_dispatch: [railway-deploy]`, which cannot work directly: GitHub's `/dispatches` endpoint authenticates by `Authorization` header and a Railway webhook cannot set one, so that route needs a PAT **and** a relay service. It is not needed — **Railway's GitHub App is already posting GitHub Deployments to this repo**: `creator: railway-app[bot]`, `environment: "routeflow / production"`, `sha` = the deployed commit, with `in_progress` → `success` statuses, verified present on every master commit back through 2026-08-28 **while the repo was private**. So `on: deployment_status` gets the identical signal with **zero secrets, zero external infrastructure and zero Railway dashboard changes**. `repository_dispatch: [railway-deploy]` stays DECLARED on ci.yml as the fallback, and was REMOVED from `post-deploy.yml` so exactly one workflow consumes it (two consumers = two Playwright suites, ~11 duplicate billed min, the first time anyone wired it). `post-deploy.yml` is now manual-only. ⚠️ **THE FRESHNESS GUARD IS NOT OPTIONAL AND MUST NOT BE "SIMPLIFIED" AWAY.** Railway posts MORE `success` events than there are deploys — measured 18 successes across the 12 most recent deployments — because when deployment N goes live Railway **re-posts `success` onto deployment N-1** (and sometimes N-2), ~4s later (19:49:41 then 19:49:45). Those carry the OLD commit as `deployment.sha`. Acting on one checks out a superseded commit, finds production correctly serving a newer one, and burns the readiness gate's full 15 min before failing: a false red AND ~17 billed min. The guard is the job's FIRST step, before the checkout, `gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/<default_branch>`; not-the-tip ⇒ `run=false` and every later step is `if:`-gated off. It never fails the job, and on an API blip it proceeds rather than skipping — a lost E2E is worse than a wasted one. ⚠️ For the same reason the e2e job's `concurrency` group is **per-SHA, deliberately not a constant**: a constant group with `cancel-in-progress` would let the stale event (arriving 4s later) CANCEL the run for the commit that actually shipped, and then skip itself — E2E would silently never run. ⚠️ `verify`'s `if:` was rewritten from `github.event_name != 'push'` to an explicit allow-list: the negative form would have run the whole correctness suite on every production deploy the moment this workflow gained a third trigger. **Same trap in the e2e gate:** `REQUIRE_SHA` was `github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'`, but on `deployment_status` `github.ref` is empty or a bare SHA, so it would have silently downgraded every deploy-triggered run to the reachability-only path while still reporting green. Both are now event-name allow-lists. `EXPECTED_SHA` and the checkout `ref:` are both `github.event.deployment.sha || github.sha` — they must stay identical or the gate's `git diff` compares the wrong trees. ⚠️ **`ci.yml` HAS NO `push:` TRIGGER ANY MORE.** Re-adding it does not make CI safer, it adds a second full-price E2E per merge; the two-line revert is spelled out in the `on:` block. **This change cannot be tested on a branch** — `deployment_status` and `repository_dispatch` only ever run the DEFAULT BRANCH's copy of a workflow, so the proof is the first master deploy after merge: if no `E2E (Playwright)` run appears within ~20 min of it, revert. PROJECTED (August volume, on top of the CI cut below): e2e 13 → **8 billed min/run**, plus ~41 min/mo of 1-minute stale-event bailouts → **~1,857 optimistic / ~2,076 central / ~2,246 conservative**, vs 2,226-2,705 before. The design quoted 1,816 because it did not know about the duplicate `success` events. Two effects it also did not price, both favourable: a FAILED Railway deploy no longer burns a 15-min gate timeout (~17 billed min) because no `success` is posted, and a SKIPPED deploy costs nothing at all. || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
